summary: Phase 7B products, verification code, manifest, and layout evidence changed after the prior audit. A separate fresh zero-context audit is required before delivery.
reviewer_reasoning: fresh zero-context run11 audit under an explicit no-subagent constraint

claim_groups.paper_text: Evidence-grounded PID and Fuzzy-PID evaluation for a 2-link manipulator.
claim_groups.evidence_value: The raw robot model has two link inertias/lengths; the deck figure is the admitted Multibody tracking artifact.

claim_groups.paper_text: Controlled payload, configuration, noise, disturbance, and actuator changes are evaluated; failed completed runs are retained; conclusions are simulation-only.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Deterministic rows cover payload/configuration/disturbance/actuator categories, stochastic rows cover noise, and all 39 deterministic, 360 stochastic, and 6 Cartesian rows are completed, including 12, 90, and 2 failures respectively; recomputed summaries include those rows.

claim_groups.paper_text: 0.001 s fixed sample time, 5.0 s nominal duration, 5001 samples, with identical plant, trajectory, limits, thresholds, and paired seeds across controllers.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Raw reference time spans 0 to 5 s in 0.001 s increments with 5001 samples; compared controllers share references, robot/scenario parameters, torque limits and success criteria; each stochastic scenario uses the same 30 seeds for all three controllers.

claim_groups.paper_text: The bounded search reduces the nominal objective by 7.283%, changes only PID gains, improves held-out objective from 0.214504 to 0.197284, and exits with flag 1 after 12 iterations and 96 evaluations.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Raw objectives are 0.202426799460455 and 0.18768375634655526, giving 7.283147860458988%; held-out values are 0.21450363216387297 and 0.19728400491642561; solver output is 12 iterations/96 evaluations with exit flag 1. Kp/Ki/Kd are the only changed controller parameters; torque limits, filter and anti-windup settings remain fixed.

claim_groups.paper_text: Manual PID, Fuzzy-PID, and optimized PID pass 8/13, 9/13, and 10/13 deterministic scenarios; the matrix has 39 runs and all three fail the combined case.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Direct grouping of 39 raw rows yields manual-pid 8/13, mamdani-fuzzy-pid 9/13, optimization-pid 10/13; the three combined-deterministic rows are completed failures. Categories map to nominal(1), payload(3), configuration(2), uncertainty(4), disturbance(1), actuator(1), combined(1).

claim_groups.paper_text: Every isolated-noise controller-scenario cell passes 30/30 paired trials, every combined-stress cell passes 0/30, and 360 trials equal 4 scenarios x 3 controllers x 30 seeds; optimized PID has the lowest high-noise error and highest mean torque slew at 2888.34 N m/s.
claim_groups.evidence_value: All nine noise-only cells are 30/30 and all three combined-stochastic cells are 0/30; the CSV has 360 rows and identical seed sets 42001-42030 per controller/scenario. At noise-high, optimized PID mean joint RMS is 0.02280767391075337 and mean torque slew is 2888.3444144176433 N m/s, respectively the lowest and highest of the controllers.

claim_groups.paper_text: All three controllers pass straight-line; only optimized PID passes pick-transfer-place; 4/6 completed runs pass and two failed completed runs remain; optimized pick-transfer-place error is 0.01422 m RMS and 0.02970 m maximum.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Raw keyed rows give three straight-line passes, one optimized pick-transfer-place pass, six completed runs, four successes and two failures. Optimized pick-transfer-place Cartesian RMS is 0.0142210111046117 m and maximum is 0.029698222399069 m.

claim_groups.paper_text: Simulink and Multibody each pass agreement and tracking for 2/2 runs, with a worst end-effector difference of 3.34e-16 m; this is model consistency, not hardware fidelity.
claim_groups.evidence_value: The two Simulink rows and two Multibody rows all have agreement/tracking pass=true. Multibody EndEffectorMax recomputes to 3.34221388864417e-16 m and MaximumOutOfPlane is 0; all evidence is simulation/model output.

claim_groups.paper_text: There is no universal winner; optimized PID is the strongest aggregate reliability baseline, with mixed nominal manual/Fuzzy-PID metrics and a torque-slew trade-off under noise.
claim_groups.evidence_value: Optimized PID leads deterministic success (10/13) and Cartesian success (2/2 versus 1/2 each), while nominal manual/Fuzzy-PID metrics split by joint/metric and optimized PID has the highest high-noise mean torque slew. The conclusion is comparative and bounded.

claim_groups.paper_text: Hardware validation, perception/task planning, collision avoidance, monitoring, and safety supervision are explicitly future work rather than completed capabilities.
claim_groups.evidence_value: The admitted evidence set contains simulation/model experiments only, and the slide frames every listed capability as a next milestone before deployment claims.

claim_groups.paper_text: The summary repeats the 2-link/0.001 s protocol, 7.283% objective reduction, optimized PID 10/13 deterministic result, 30/30 versus 0/30 stochastic contrast, strongest aggregate reliability conclusion, and simulation-only limitations.
claim_groups.evidence_value: DOCX structure and current one-page PDF text match the resolved package. Recomputed raw values are two links, 0.001 s, 7.283147860458988%, 10/13, and per-cell 30/30 versus 0/30; the aggregate conclusion and limitations match groups 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 9.
